3.9.name: 3.09.md
3.9.text:
```cpp
string s;
cout << s[0] << endl;
```

According to the string class' definition, default initializing s will return an empty string, i.e. a string that contains no characters except for the null character '\0'.

Thus, s[0] will return the null character '\0'. Given that it is a non-graphical character, cout will not print it.

Although the above is a valid C++ code, modifying s[0] will cause undefined behaviour. Moreover, it is considered good practice to initialize objects explicitly, as opposed to relaying on the class' default initialization.

To achieve the desired result of advancing mid to a point with the container, we must advance beg by n elements (see table 3.7). This is achieved by the expression beg + (end - beg) / 2. Note that unlike addition, subtracting two iterators yields the distance between the iterators, not a reference.

3.34.name: 3.34.md
3.34.text:
```cpp
p1 += p2 - p1;
```

Find the distance between p1 and p2 and add it to p1. Essentially, this code moves p1 to the position of p2. Provided that both pointers point to memory locations within the boundaries of the same array (or 1 past the last element) , the code will always be legal.
